notes: output_file must name an entry of the document's output_files; GetOutputFileConfig returns nil otherwise and the config is rejected. A cross-document reference: expressible in the schema only as a string.
type=merge_files requires input_channel.type=stage.
Exactly one: both set is an error, neither is an error. The if/then overlay can express this; (applicable, required) cannot.
prompt_template_name must match the key of a prompt_templates entry of the document. Cross-document, so the schema can only type it as a string.

provenance_schema_name must name a provenance/<name>.pv.json of the workspace whose own key equals the name; the document is outside the config entirely, so neither the schema nor the config validator can see it. When that document declares a response_format it is adopted if the operator has none and compared if it has one, and a difference is refused - which is the whole of why the two copies stop being able to drift (agentic_ai I-438).

An operator naming a provenance schema needs exactly one column_encodings entry on the channel spec its input and output share: that column is the serialised entity the prompt was built from and is what the answer is grounded against. Zero and two are both refused at build - zero would report every field unsupported on every record, two would ground against a column the prompt may not have carried. The spec belongs to the document channels section, so no fragment-level check can see it.

Every output_mapping.column must be a column of the shared input/output channel spec. Needs the channel spec, so neither the schema nor the config validator can check it; the operator builder does, at DAG-build time. Recorded here rather than on OllamaSpec because output_channel is only reachable from the transformation.

CORRECTED at B.3: the comment implied mutual exclusion, but the builder takes the native factory first and lets use_jet_rules_go overwrite it - the Go engine wins when both are set. Both false selects the default factory (pipe_transformation_jetrules.go:92-93).
Both may be empty when column_name_fragments is used.
A stage output channel must say where to write: write_step_id names the staging step, file_key an explicit location. Found by the B.7 harness.

The sort key: domain_key resolves through the source's domain key spec, sort_by names columns directly; with neither the operator emitted records in arrival order. Found via the B.14 unknown-key audit (a dead `expr` key carried the intended sort column in two production configs).

An output channel setting both use_original_headers and put_headers_on_first_partition gets the header line of its final merged file from the first stage part file upstream — the merge concatenates the part files by s3 multipart copy without rewriting them — so every stage channel on the path leading to it, followed backward through read_step_id/write_step_id, must set both flags as well. Cross-step, so neither the schema nor a per-fragment check can express it.
Every sort_by member must be a column of the input channel; an unknown name rejects the DAG build (pipe_transformation_sort.go:110). Invisible to the config validator, so the prompt must carry it.
domain_key resolves through the main input source domain key spec; a missing spec or an unknown key rejects the DAG build (pipe_transformation_sort.go:95,102).
Same resolution as the sort operator: through the main input source domain key spec, rejected at DAG build when missing or unknown (pipe_transformation_group_by.go:118,128).

The merge operator must be the first operator of the step: its extra sources are the first pipe's input_channel.merge_channels (pipe_transformation_merge.go:211), and every merge source must carry a domain key spec (:258). Positional and cross-section, so only the prompt can carry it.

Under the merge operator both set is rejected - the opposite of the group_by operator, where name silently wins over pos. Applies equally to each merge_group_by entry; both flow through MakeHashExpressionFromGroupByConfig.
The merge key: one of the three must be set or the build is rejected. group_by_pos entries are range-checked against the source columns (pipe_transformation_merge.go:312).

filter_columns.lookup_name must name a defined lookup table - checked by the validator at startup; lookup_column and column_name must then be columns of that table, checked at DAG build (pipe_transformation_shuffling.go:101,105).

The named channel's spec must carry the five correlation columns: column_name_1, column_name_2, observations_count, distinct_column_1_count, distinct_column_2_count (pipe_transformation_clustering.go:103-121).
When set, the name (after env substitution) must be a non-empty mapping in the jetsapi database - outside the document entirely, so neither the schema nor the config validator can see it.

Each jetrules output channel must resolve in the registry and its channel spec must carry a class_name - the exported rdf type (pipe_transformation_jetrules.go:134-135). The validator separately requires the channel_spec_name and checks the column encodings.

Every member must be a column of the input channel; an unknown name rejects the DAG build (pipe_transformation_group_by.go:141). Until 2026-08-16 an unknown name silently grouped by column 0 - the hazard the B.3 sweep recorded, now closed in the builder. Mirrors the sort_by rule.
